# Preprocessing report (generated by scripts/step1_preprocess.py)

Source: `india_housing_prices.csv` with 250,000 rows and 23 columns. After cleaning: 250,000 rows and 42 columns.

## 1. Data-quality checks

| Check | Result | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Missing values (all columns) | 0 | Median / mode imputation is built in, so new data is handled safely |
| Duplicate rows (ignoring ID) | 0 (0.0%) | Dropped |
| Duplicate IDs | 0 (0.0%) | None to fix |
| Price or size <= 0 | 0 (0.0%) | None to fix |
| Year_Built outside 1900-2025 | 0 (0.0%) | None to fix |
| Age_of_Property != 2025 - Year_Built | 0 (0.0%) | Age is recomputed anyway |
| Price_per_SqFt shown as 0.00 (rounded lakhs) | 2,534 (1.0%) | Recomputed in rupees from price and size |
| Price_per_SqFt differs from price / size by more than 0.01 lakh | 0 (0.0%) | Recomputed in rupees |
| Floor_No higher than Total_Floors | 116,304 (46.5%) | Flagged in Floor_Invalid, then capped at the top floor |
| Layout below 250 sqft per BHK (for example 500 sqft, 5 BHK) | 16,816 (6.7%) | Reported only; kept because size and BHK are both valid values |
| Parking_Space / Security not Yes or No | 0 (0.0%) | None to fix |
| Unknown amenity names | 0 (0.0%) | None to fix |
| Category labels changed by trimming spaces | 0 columns | Whitespace is stripped in every text column |

## 3. Outliers (IQR rule, 1.5 x IQR)

| Column | Outlier rows | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Price (lakhs) | 0 | 0.0% |
| Size (sqft) | 0 | 0.0% |
| Price per sqft (Rs, recomputed) | 19,723 | 7.9% |
| Nearby schools | 0 | 0.0% |
| Nearby hospitals | 0 | 0.0% |

Outliers are flagged (`PPS_Outlier`, `Size_Outlier`) and kept. A copy of price per sqft trimmed at the 1st and 99th percentile (`Price_per_SqFt_W`) is available for modelling.

## 4. Encoding and scaling

- Scaled with z-scores in `processed_housing.csv`: Size_in_SqFt, Price_in_Lakhs, Price_per_SqFt, Year_Built, Age_of_Property, Floor_No, Total_Floors, Nearby_Schools, Nearby_Hospitals, Sqft_per_BHK, City_Median_PPS, City_BHK_Median_Price, Amenity_Count.
- One-hot encoded: Property_Type, Facing, Owner_Type. Ordinal: Furnished_Status (0 to 2) and Public_Transport_Accessibility (1 to 3). Yes/No columns become 0/1.
- During model training the encoder and scaler are fitted on the training rows only, inside the pipeline, so the test set never leaks into preprocessing.
